rules.title: Annual rent increase cap for Newark rent-controlled dwellings
rules.requirement: For covered housing spaces, a landlord may not increase rent at lease expiration or termination of a periodic tenancy by more than the stated CPI formula, capped at 4%, and may not increase rent more than that in any consecutive twelve-month period regardless of vacancy, new tenant, or ownership change. The landlord must give the tenant and Rent Regulation Officer at least 30 days’ written notice, and no annual increase, tax surcharge, major new improvement surcharge, or hardship increase is allowed unless the dwelling is in substantial compliance and registration requirements are met.
rules.key_value: CPI increase from 15 months prior to 3 months prior, max 4%, in any consecutive 12-month period

coverage.other_unresolvable: Exemptions depend on use or program status, including public housing, transient hotel or motel space, commercial use, certain rehabilitated subsidized units, government-agency rent regulation contracts, and newly constructed or vacant dwellings as set forth elsewhere in the chapter.
coverage.summary: Applies to all multiple dwellings and housing spaces in Newark subject to the chapter, except listed exempt dwellings.

rules.exemptions: Exempt dwellings include public housing; motel or hotel space rented day-to-day to transients; commercial space; newly constructed multiple dwellings and vacant dwellings as set forth in Subsections 19:2-18.1 and 19:2-18.2; units rehabilitated by specified federal and state rental rehabilitation programs receiving Section 8 subsidies or federal vouchers during the subsidy/program tenure, with rents not exceeding HUD fair market rents; and rents regulated under a governmental-agency contract where that agency’s authority supersedes Newark’s authority during the contract period.
rules.penalty: A landlord must rebate rent collected above the chapter’s permissible amount by crediting the tenant over a period not to exceed 14 months, or refunding within one month if the tenant is no longer in occupancy; the rebate is retroactive to two years from the petition date.
rules.interaction: The chapter states that where a governmental-agency contract supersedes Newark’s authority to regulate the rent, the chapter is preempted during that contract period, but applies before the contract begins and immediately after it terminates.
rules.quoted_span:
At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease
     of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in
     the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI 15 months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase
     to the CPI three months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase.
